messages:
From: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>
To: Liam O'Connor <liam.oconnor@brighthelm.com>, Rina Patel <rina.patel@brighthelm.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 18 Nov 2026 15:02:00 -0800
Subject: Post-demo recap & proposed POC lane (success criteria + next steps)

Hi Liam / Rina —

Thanks again for the call today. Quick recap + proposed next steps so we’re all aligned before we kick off the POC:

Summary of ask
- Evaluate Redwood inference for product-recommendation reranking and cart-assist flows (latency-sensitive; 99th pct target 120ms).
- Provide judgment on production fit within a 4-week technical POC.

Success criteria (Brighthelm acceptance gates)
1) Latency: median < 60ms and 99th < 120ms for 1–2 token responses under target QPS (see perf targets below).
2) Quality: NDCG@10 improvement >= 8% on provided evaluation set compared to current baseline.
3) Integration: end-to-end inference working via SDK or REST streaming without schema changes to product record.
4) Data handling: no product or PII retention beyond per-request KV caching; audit logs accessible.

Proposed technical plan & timeline
- Week 0 (this week): Access — provide sandbox API key, dataset sample (5k queries), and an engineer contact for data access.
- Week 1: Quick integration spike (SDK + streaming) — basic inference calls, tokenization sanity check.
- Week 2: Run workload ramp & perf tuning (batching/quant profiles).
- Week 3: Evaluation run (NDCG) + final perf validation.
- Week 4: Acceptance & recommendations + handoff notes.

Ownership
- Redwood: Kim (sales) + Ben (solutions) + Marcus (integration eng) — technical handoff + performance tuning.
- Brighthelm: Liam (eng lead) + Brighthelm Eng contact for dataset/credentials.

Blocking items we need from Brighthelm
- Short list of 5k sample queries + expected baseline metrics (precision / NDCG baseline).
- Dedicated eng contact and reachable Slack channel.
- Confirmation that trial traffic can flow to sandbox endpoints (allowed IP ranges).

Attachments: redwood-poc-api-spec-v1.pdf (stub), mutual-action-plan.xlsx (stub) — both contain the SDK quickstart and required headers.

Next step: Liam — can you confirm dataset delivery and nailing down an eng contact by EOD Friday? Once confirmed we’ll schedule the Week 1 kickoff.

Thanks,

Kimberly Park
Director, Solutions — Redwood Inference

Looping Marcus for two quick tech clarifications so we can scope the Week 1 spike:

Marcus — can you confirm the minimal integration paths we should prioritize for a fast spike? My suggestions:
1) REST synchronous route (POST /v1/infer) — no streaming, simplest to validate tokenization and quality.
2) gRPC/HTTP2 streaming route — for reranking at low latency; we should test continuous batching behavior under our sandbox QPS.
3) SDK wrapper (node/python) — sample snippet so Brighthelm can call with 1–2 lines (we have the quickstart in the attached spec).

Also: do we need any special schema/protobuf changes for the tool-calling variant they mentioned (product-enrichment tool call)? If so, call it out and we'll include a 1-day work estimate in the MLP.

Marcus: any risks or config knobs we should surface now (quantization choices, kv-cache TTL, prefix caching recommendations)?

-Ben

Thanks everyone — consolidated technical plan and owners below (kickoff Tue 24 Nov confirmed by Liam):

Week 1 (spike) — owners: Marcus (lead), Rohan (Brighthelm eng)
- Deliverables: SDK quickstart (node + python) + sample repo link; REST POST /v1/infer example; streaming example with a small client script.
- Acceptance to move forward: Brighthelm can run the sample repo end-to-end against a Redwood sandbox key and see valid inference responses for 100 queries.

Week 2 (ramp & profiling) — owners: Marcus + Ben
- Deliverables: load profile run (target QPS 20 sustained, 50 bursts), profiler logs, suggested batching/quantization config.
- Tasks: enable prefix caching for frequently-seen user-query prefixes; instrument 95/99 latency histograms.

Week 3 (evaluation) — owners: Marissa + Liam + Rohan
- Deliverables: NDCG calculation script (we will run against the 5k sample), final perf run, recommendation doc.

Week 4 (acceptance & handoff) — owners: Kimberly + Rina
- Deliverables: POC acceptance memo, small SOW for production pilot if accepted.

Implementation specifics (technical notes):
- REST: POST /v1/infer (body: {model, input, context_id}), auth: Bearer sandbox-key. Example included in redwood-poc-api-spec-v1.pdf (stub).
- Streaming: gRPC/HTTP2 with chunked token frames — recommend client-side 50ms read timeout; we will provide a small client example.
- Tool calling: product-enrichment hooks will be exposed as a separate endpoint /v1/tool-call with signed callback handshake. Brighthelm should expose a callback URL and a short HMAC secret so we can validate callbacks during the spike.
- Data handling: ephemeral KV cache only; audit logs exported to a pre-shared S3 (read-only) during the POC.

Open items (action owner, due)
- Brighthelm: share 5k sample + baseline metrics (Liam) — due 2026-11-24 (confirmed).
- Brighthelm: provide sandbox IP CIDR for whitelist (Liam) — due 2026-11-24.
- Redwood: send short SOW for POC (Kim/Rina) — due 2026-11-25.
- Redwood: SDK quickstart + sample repo (Marcus/Marissa) — internal target 2026-11-24 EOD.

If this looks good I’ll attach links to the sample repo and the quickstart in Drive.

-Marissa
